findings.finding: The --declared-complexity CLI option has no production caller (the runner passes only --spec); declared = declared_complexity is a no-op alias.
findings.suggestion: Remove the option and the merge list; use the parameter directly.

findings.finding: classify() does not validate declared_complexity when called directly; apply_floor fails with an opaque ValueError while recheck() names the problem.
findings.suggestion: Validate in apply_floor so both entry points raise the same named error.

findings.finding: Parser accepted only spaces and ignored trailing punctuation; a scope line such as Complexity: TBD or Complexity: large in free text could fail or floor a unit.
findings.suggestion: Allow tabs, treat trailing punctuation as malformed, scan only the header before the first level-2 heading, add tests.

findings.finding: The noqa F401 on the _split_flags import is misleading because main() calls it directly.

Claim under doubt: a unit declared medium in the brief can no longer be recorded small — The floor exists only if the orchestrator copies the brief tier into a complexity key when it calls campaign_init; wording said may carry and nothing checks the copy. A missing key reads as undeclared and passes F11.
findings.suggestion: Make the wording mandatory, or record each unit declared tier in campaign.md so the setup review shows the omission.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: the runner always passes --spec — A runner launched from the stale plugin cache uses the old contract without --spec; declared_complexity is null and F11 cannot tell undeclared from omitted.
findings.suggestion: Record that a spec was consulted, or state that the post-merge cache sync is mandatory before any campaign dispatch.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: a spec with no declaration behaves exactly as before — The parser searched the whole spec, so free scope or acceptance-criteria text such as Complexity: large or Complexity: TBD could raise the tier or hard-fail a unit; a malformed header line was skipped when a valid line appeared later.
findings.suggestion: Parse only the header region and let the first declaring line decide.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: the floor is local to campaign units — F5c entries recorded at the declared floor feed the history-prior median used by standalone iterates.
findings.suggestion: Accept in writing or exclude declared-sourced entries.

findings.finding: The docstring claims "a later quotation of the format inside the spec cannot override the header," but `search()` returns the first full-line match anywhere in the file. A hand-edited or pre-existing unit spec (which the module explicitly supports — "every hand-written or pre-existing unit") that quotes or fences an example `Complexity:` line above the real header silently replaces the operator's floor with the quoted value (e.g. a fenced `Complexity: small` above `Complexity: medium` drops the floor back to `small` — exactly the silent-drop failure this change exists to close). Conversely, a fenced example in a unit that declares none silently fabricates a floor. glm's external review explicitly called out code fences; the strict full-line regex addresses typos but not position/fencing.
findings.suggestion: Ignore content inside fenced code blocks when scanning, or prefer the highest-ranked / last declaring line, or only accept a declaration from the header region of the spec. Add a parse test for "quotation before header" and "fenced example in an undeclared unit."

findings.finding: Any line in the spec consisting solely of `complexity: <single-word>` is treated as a malformed declaration and raises `ValueError`, which now exits 2 in both CLIs. But hand-written scope text can legitimately contain such a line as ordinary prose — e.g. a bullet `- complexity: quadratic` or `- complexity: high` in a performance note — with no intent to declare a tier. That hard-stops the whole unit run on non-declaration prose. (Multi-word values like `n/a` or `small changes are fine` fall through to `None`, so the strictness is also inconsistent across prose shapes.)
findings.suggestion: Scope the malformed-level error to lines outside code fences, or only raise when a well-formed declaring line also exists elsewhere / the line appears in the header region; otherwise treat single-word non-level lines as prose.

findings.finding: For a record with an unknown declared tier (`huge`), the failure message tells the operator to "Re-run the Step 3.4 re-check with --spec" — but re-running with `--spec` cannot fix a corrupted record; the correct remedy is fixing the record/spec's malformed line. Cosmetic in a message that gates a hard failure.
findings.suggestion: Differentiate the message for `decl_rank is None` ("invalid declared tier in the record — fix the spec's Complexity line") from the genuine below-floor case.

findings.finding: The parser searches for any valid declaration before checking malformed declarations.
